cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing a letter to Timothy. He opens with grace, mercy and peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord. Friend, that's not a hello. That's a whole CARE PACKAGE.

cards.question: Paul says he's an apostle of Christ Jesus. By whose command?

answers.text: God our Savior and Christ Jesus

cards.question: At the top of the letter, Paul calls Timothy his true ___ in the faith.

cards.text: As a Papa myself, that true child line gets me right in the apron. Then Paul gets down to business: when he left for Macedonia, he urged Timothy to stay on in one city.

cards.question: Which city did Paul urge Timothy to stay on in?
Timothy is supposed to instruct certain men in that city to stop doing something. What is it?

cards.text: These men are also hooked on myths and endless genealogies. ENDLESS, friend, like the dead batteries I shared that drawer with, arguing for YEARS over who had the most charge left.

cards.question: Paul says those myths and endless genealogies promote ___ rather than the stewardship of God's work.

cards.text: So what's the goal of all this instruction anyway? Paul tells Timothy straight out.

cards.question: What does Paul say is the goal of his instruction?

cards.text: Love that comes from a pure heart, a clear conscience and a sincere faith. But some people have strayed from all that and turned aside to empty talk.

cards.question: The people who turned aside to empty talk want to be teachers of the ___.
Paul says these would-be teachers of the law understand what they're saying.

cards.text: And they say it all so confidently. You know the type, friend: the guy in the group chat explaining traffic laws with his WHOLE chest who has never once driven a car.
So is the law itself the problem here? Hold on, friend, Paul clears that right up.

cards.question: What does Paul say about the law itself?

answers.text: It is good if used rightly
It has been done away with
It is too heavy to carry

cards.question: Paul says the law is enacted for the righteous.

cards.text: The law is for the lawless and rebellious, and Paul keeps going down a long list: the ungodly and sinful, murderers, the sexually immoral, slave traders, liars and more. He ends it with anyone else who is averse to sound teaching.

cards.question: What does Paul say that sound teaching agrees with?

answers.text: The glorious gospel of the blessed God
The traditions handed down by the elders
The wisdom of the Greek teachers

cards.question: Paul says he has been entrusted with that glorious gospel.

findings.problem: The opening card has four sentences: "Paul, an apostle... to Timothy." / "He opens with grace..." / "Friend, that's not a hello." / "That's a whole CARE PACKAGE." The limit is three.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on.

findings.problem: Timothy appears here for the first time, but the card doesn't say who he is. Paul gets "an apostle of Christ Jesus," while Timothy is only named. Any intro has to avoid giving away card 3's answer ("child"). A cited outside fact like Paul's coworker (Acts 16:1-3) would work.

rule.text: New people. The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The setup "So is the law itself the problem here? Hold on, friend, Paul clears that right up" signals that the law is not the problem. That rules out card 16's wrong answers "It has been done away with" and "It is too heavy to carry." Both of those treat the law as the problem.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Timothy 1:8 but tells nothing from that verse. It is only a teaser question, so it doesn't carry a moment of the passage.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The card cites 1 Timothy 1:10-11, but its right answer, "The glorious gospel of the blessed God," comes only from 1:11. The "sound teaching" in 1:10 is in the question, not the answer. The citation should be 1 Timothy 1:11.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.
